_comment: CC Post Sepia Alpha — turns a [C-MAPMARK] render (sepia ink on pure white) into a transparent map sprite. The blue channel separates warm brown ink from white paper better than luminance does: paper ~1.0, umber ink ~0.15. InvertMask gives ink coverage, MaskComposite add doubles it so mid-tone washes go fully opaque and only the paper stays clear, InvertMask again because JoinImageWithAlpha reads 1 = transparent. No BiRefNet: a line drawing has no silhouette for a cutout model to find, and the doubled coverage keeps the brush's soft edges semi-transparent. ImageCrop then trims to the drawing's own alpha bounding box (post.py scans the render and fills the slots) — a side-elevation symbol fills anywhere from 47% to 77% of the square, so without the trim the frame's empty margin, not the drawing, would set how big it lands on the map. ImageScale takes width 0 to keep the trimmed aspect and size by height. post.py --tier mark drives it.

_meta.title: Blue channel: white paper 1.0, umber ink ~0.15
Coverage x2 (clamped): mid-tone fills go opaque, paper stays clear
Trim to the drawing's alpha bounding box
Resize by height, width 0 keeps the trimmed aspect (lanczos)
